# NURAE

> NURAE is a self-hostable platform for creating, hosting and operating AI-powered
> Telegram bots — describe a bot in plain language and NURAE compiles, hosts and
> runs it. Built by FRAZIYM TECH & AI.

NURAE is designed to be operated by AI agents as much as by humans. Agents build
bots, configure behavior, and run the platform itself through audited tool layers.

## What bots can do (the behavior DSL)

A bot is described in behaviors — plain-language units the compiler turns into
Telegram commands, inline keyboards, callbacks and flows:

- Triggers: start, /commands, keyword ("says"), button presses, deep-link payloads,
  group member joins, anything-else fallback (AI or static).
- Steps: messages with buttons, media, polls/quizzes, Telegram Stars payments,
  collect-and-remember forms, AI steps with conversation memory, reminders,
  silent counters (remember/add), random draws, leaderboards.
- Growth primitives: channel join-gates (verify_join), daily streaks, milestone
  celebrations, referral deep links with automatic credit, consent-first email
  invitations (double opt-in, permanent unsubscribe).

## For AI agents and MCP clients

- Tool manifest (MCP-compatible): `GET /api/agents/tools` — the full tool
  registry as JSON-schema descriptors (kind: read/write, consequential flags),
  plus the SKILL LIBRARY: named playbooks (build-from-brief, order-form-alerts,
  shop-with-stars, reminders-drip, grow-audience, diagnose-bot, audience-outreach,
  polish-copy · operator: morning-brief, fleet-health, diagnose-down-bot,
  customer-review, settings-change). Agents read a playbook with `skill_read`
  and follow it step by step.
- Bot Builder agent: a signed-in user's agent that builds and manages THEIR bots
  through that registry (drafts, behaviors, publishing, broadcasts, schedules).
- Operator agent: the instance admin's platform agent — server overview, fleet
  management, any bot's configuration, site settings, customers, logs and
  analytics (admin-token authenticated, audit-logged).
- Health: `GET /api/health` — `{ status, version, name, vendor }`.

## Integration notes

- Identity always comes from the authenticated session, admin token or Bearer
  AgentToken — never from model output. Consequential actions require an
  explicit human approval flag.
- Bots follow the Telegram Bot API honestly: no first-contact DMs (the API
  refuses), no unsolicited email (consent-first only). Growth comes from
  join-gates, streaks, referral loops and shareable deep links.
- Owner instant alerts: a bot owner registers their own Telegram chat id
  (bot_set_owner_chat / bot page) and every completed order, intake form and
  Stars payment is pushed to their Telegram the moment it happens.
- Self-hosting: one Node process + SQLite; point NURAE_SITE_URL at the public
  origin, add a Telegram token per bot, an AI provider key (OpenRouter has free
  models), and the fleet + agents wake up on their own.

## Remote API

External AI agents (e.g. Claude) can operate NURAE directly over Bearer
AgentTokens. Mint them in the NURAE dashboard (API keys card) — the raw key
(`nrae_…`) is shown once, only its hash is stored, revocation is instant.

- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer nrae_…`. Identity comes from the token, never
  from the request body. User-scope tokens act as their owner; platform-scope
  tokens (operator only) unlock the platform tool tier.
- `GET /api/v1/me` — token identity (name, scope, owner email).
- `GET /api/v1/tools` — the tool registry as JSON-schema descriptors + the
  skill library; platform scope also gets `platformTools` + `operatorSkills`.
- `POST /api/v1/tools/call` — `{tool, args?, confirm?}` → always HTTP 200 with
  `{ok, status: "ok"|"error"|"confirm", label, detail?, data?}`. Consequential
  tools (publish, unpublish, broadcast) answer `status: "confirm"` and DO NOT
  run until the human approves; then resend with `confirm: true`. Tokens
  minted with allowConsequential=false can never execute them.
- `POST /api/v1/agent/turn` — `{text, sessionId?, attachmentIds?}` → one full
  Bot Builder turn (`{sessionId, reply, steps, done}`). User-scope tokens
  only; approvals still happen in the web UI. Limits: 20 turns/min.
- `POST /api/mcp` — MCP connector surface (JSON-RPC 2.0): `initialize`,
  `notifications/initialized` (202), `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Missing auth
  → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- `GET /api/openapi.json` — the machine-readable contract (OpenAPI 3.1).
- Limits: 60 tool calls/min and 20 agent turns/min per token. Every call is
  audit-logged; secrets (bot tokens, AI keys) are never returned.

## Vendor

FRAZIYM TECH & AI — NURAE, build, run and improve AI Telegram bots.
